topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of cancer susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as the evolution of mutation-bearing cells whose growth depends on their biological context.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and the evidence for their contribution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the contribution of environmental exposures to cancer risk and how evidence about that contribution is interpreted.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example of interacting infectious causes.

topics.label: Mechanisms of DNA damage from environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage through mechanisms shaped by their chemical properties and processing within the body.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutation-producing initiation from the promotional conditions that allow initiated cells to proliferate into tumours.

topics.label: Developmental and tissue-specific susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the biological context of exposure determines susceptibility to carcinogens and consolidate the preceding account of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Methods and limitations for assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence linking exposures to cancer is obtained and why available assessment methods have important limitations.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture's conclusions around the difficulty of assessing cancer risks and weighing them against benefits.
